The official Teams integration roadmap is a controlled, future-dated release: the integration is under “Active Design and Planning” with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November), a restricted pilot beginning October 2026 for selected financial/healthcare accounts, and a required security architecture using Azure AD tokens and role-token enforcement [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. The official roadmap also states that only the Slack connector is currently available as a limited pilot, and it explicitly warns that sales playbooks or informal Slack threads may suggest the Teams integration is “ready for deployment” or “nearly complete” when it is not [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. The sales playbook instructs reps to treat the roadmap as the source of truth, not to guarantee launch dates, and confirms the Teams integration is in planning/design for Q4 2026 [NL-009#NL-009-S08]. Management reporting likewise describes the Teams integration as “in the design and planning phase, scheduled for Q4 2026” and notes sales pressure to overclaim readiness [NL-016#NL-016-S05].

By contrast, informal sales and Slack claims overstate readiness. In a sales call, Marcus Reed told the customer the Teams integration is “basically right around the corner,” “almost ready for general release,” and could be turned on for a July pilot via an “early access build” – a claim explicitly flagged as a “significant sales overclaim” against the official roadmap [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. In internal Slack, Marcus Reed said Teams was “basically right around the corner,” asked for a pilot by July or August, proposed packaging the “toy bot” as an “alpha” for a customer, and even proposed a custom hardcoded build [NL-027#NL-027-S04], [NL-027#NL-027-S02]. Engineering and product staff rejected these proposals, stating the Teams integration is in design for Q4, that the existing demo is a “toy” with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero citation formatting, and that releasing it would be a security and SOC 2 risk [NL-027#NL-027-S03], [NL-027#NL-027-S04]. The CTO and Product VP also refused to pull resources from the OCR pipeline to accelerate Teams, keeping the integration in design for Q4 with development in early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

Resolution: the official roadmap has higher authority than informal sales/Slack claims, which are explicitly contradicted as overclaims. The available evidence is sufficient to conclude the Teams integration is not ready for general release or July/August pilots as informally claimed; the official status is design/planning with a Q4 2026 target and an October 2026 restricted pilot.
